correctness.rationale: The symmetry classification is exhaustive (one axis-fixed vertex and two reflected pairs); side-length constraints plus convexity yield exactly 1/4 <= x <= 1. The edge-normal width principle and explicit support-dot-product computations yield the three exact candidates. Complete analytic comparisons on three closed subintervals show the unique endpoint maximum. Rational sign inequalities are displayed, and endpoint S=9+2 sqrt(3), w=sqrt(3)/2 are reconstructed. The 30,001 numeric checks do not substitute for a proof.

value.rationale: The natural sum-over-all-vertex-pairs divided by minimum width is the fourth, numerically motivated extremal problem in the Audet–Ninin program. The predicted trapezoidal extremizer is itself reflection-symmetric, making the symmetric pentagon case mathematically motivated rather than an arbitrary slice. The result gives the exact sharp constant, unique weak equality and strict-class supremum, a meaningful analytic partial resolution; it does not assert the unrestricted conjecture.
